surprise.title: 31 years ago today, Toy Story became the first movie made entirely by computer
surprise.body: Toy Story opened across the United States on November 22, 1995, three days after its premiere at the El Capitan Theatre, and it was the first feature film animated entirely on computers. It grew out of Tin Toy, a 1988 Pixar short told from a toy's point of view, made at a studio Steve Jobs had bought in 1986. The numbers behind it are wild for the era: 114,240 frames across 1,561 shots, about 800,000 machine hours, and a render farm of Sun Microsystems computers running around the clock, yet Pixar could finish less than 30 seconds of film per day. Each frame was rendered at just 1536 by 922 pixels with Pixar's own RenderMan software, then recorded onto film stock. On a $30 million budget it earned about $401 million, became the first animated film nominated for Best Original Screenplay, received a Special Achievement Academy Award, and entered the National Film Registry in 2005. Today is overcast and dry in Tallahassee, around 60 to 64 degrees with sunset at 5:37 PM, which makes for a fine rewatch afternoon. Twenty-one days until you sail on December 13.
